newsitem.title: BURKINA FASO: Nigeria's Abacha confirms 1998 presidential poll.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria's Abacha confirms 1998 presidential poll.

text.p: Nigerian President Sani Abacha, returning to the international scene after being shunned over human rights abuses, confirmed on Thursday the schedule for return to democratic rule by 1998, French official sources said.
They said Abacha had a 30-minute private meeting with French President Jacques Chirac during the Franco-African summit in the Burkina Fasso capital Ouagadougou.
They said Abacha confirmed plans for municipal and federal elections leading in 1998 to elections for the National Assembly and a presidential poll.
It was the first time Nigeria had been invited to a Franco-African summit, now enlarged to include a dozen English-speaking African countries.

Abacha's military government has faced international outcry over human rights abuses and lack of progress towards democracy. The Commonwealth suspended it a year ago over the hanging of nine minority rights activists including author Ken Saro-Wiwa.
The Nigerian leader showered praise on Chirac as he addressed a gala dinner winding up the summit in his role as president of the Economic Community of West African States.
He expressed "deep appreciation" for Chirac's "endearing and continuous commitment" to the development of Africa.
The sources said Chirac and Abacha also discussed Nigeria's territorial dispute with Cameroon over the Bakassi peninsula.

Chirac urged Abacha to settle the dispute peacefully through the International Court of Justice in the Hague. It was not clear whether Abacha met Cameroon officials during the summit, which Cameroon President Paul Biya did not attend.
